thesis: Abercrombie & Fitch reported Q2 on Aug 26 with record net sales of $1.27B, up 5% and a 15th consecutive quarter of growth, diluted EPS of $4.17 against $1.99 consensus, and raised full-year EPS guidance to $13.10-$13.60 from $10.20-$11.00. The shares gained roughly 35-42% on the day. The read is discounted by how the beat was produced: an approximately $100M pre-tax refund of tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, booked as a reduction to cost of sales, which on 44.4M shares accounts for essentially the entire $2.18 EPS beat and much of the guidance raise. That is a mechanical, non-recurring item rather than a change in the underlying 5% sales trajectory. Separately, former CEO Mike Jeffries faces a 16-count DOJ indictment filed in October 2024 with trial set for Oct 26, 2026. This suggests entering after a one-day repricing of that size, on a beat that is largely a one-off, carries poor reward for the risk.
invalidation: A subsequent quarter shows the raised guidance holding on operating performance without further tariff-refund benefit, or the shares retrace toward the pre-print level while sales growth stays near 5%.
sources: Top Class Actions (Jeffries indictment and Oct 26 2026 trial date): https://topclassactions.com/lawsuit-settlements/investigations/abercrombie-and-fitch-former-ceo-class-action-lawsuit/

thesis: Intel's disclosed operating results have turned: Q2 2026 revenue rose 25.4% to $16.1B on data-centre demand, and the company guided Q3 to $16.3B, up 19% year over year and roughly 8% above the $15.1B FactSet consensus. On Aug 25 it also unveiled the Diamond Rapids, Crescent Island and Wildcat Lake processors aimed at enterprise, data-centre AI and edge workloads. Against that, the completed $20B upsized equity offering priced at $95 on Aug 10 leaves an unabsorbed supply overhang with the stock at $88.26, still below what allocators paid, and the raise is real dilution rather than a funding announcement. The offsetting point is that the dilution funds precisely the data-centre and foundry capacity producing the revenue acceleration, and the shares sit 22.6% above the 200-day MA of $72.00 while 38% below the 52-week high. This suggests the operating trajectory now supports exposure, with the overhang as the live risk rather than the thesis.
invalidation: Q3 revenue misses the $16.3B guide, the shares fail to reclaim the $95 offering price and break back below the 200-day MA, or a further equity raise is announced.
sources: Benzinga (Diamond Rapids / Crescent Island / Wildcat Lake): https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/08/61403232/intel-unveils-next-gen-ai-processors-to-drive-enterprise-and-data-center-growth
Stock Analysis (INTC quote and Q2/Q3 figures): https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/intc/

thesis: Biohaven signed a global licensing and collaboration agreement with SK Biopharmaceuticals on Aug 26 covering its Kv7 ion-channel platform and opakalim (BHV-7000), with total deal value of $795M, and the shares rose about 13-15% on roughly 6x average volume. That is a signed, company-disclosed agreement and it brings non-dilutive capital to a company that cut R&D spending 60% after the FDA issued a complete response letter for troriluzole in spinocerebellar ataxia. The balance-sheet position remains the binding constraint: Q2 2026 net loss of $137.3M and a six-month loss of $267.8M, less than a year of cash runway on current free cash flow, shares outstanding up 30% over the past year, and a newly added omnibus shelf registration covering common equity, debt and hybrid securities. A $795M headline deal value is milestone-weighted, not cash in hand. This suggests the licensing win improves the outlook without resolving the funding gap that a shelf registration exists to close.
invalidation: Upfront cash from the SK agreement is disclosed at a level that funds operations past the current runway, or a financing is completed on terms that remove the near-term dilution question.
sources: Fierce Biotech (troriluzole CRL and 60% R&D cut): https://www.fiercebiotech.com/biotech/fda-rejects-biohaven-approval-request-triggering-cost-cutting

Simply Wall St (runway, 30% share increase, shelf registration): https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/pharmaceuticals-biotech/nyse-bhvn/biohaven/news/biohaven-bhvn-narrows-loss-and-adds-shelf-registration-is-it/amp

thesis: Kanzhun reported Q2 on Aug 25 with revenue of RMB2.4B, up 14% year over year, an adjusted operating margin of 43.8%, up 1.9 points, and average monthly active users on BOSS Zhipin above 70 million for the first time. The company has completed more than $300M of buybacks year to date and total 2026 shareholder returns exceed $530M, more than 100% of 2025 adjusted net income, and it guided Q3 revenue to RMB2.41-2.50B for 11.4-15.6% growth. These are disclosed results rather than projections. Two things keep this from a stronger read: the Q3 guide brackets rather than extends the 14% growth rate, so the acceleration case is unproven, and a shareholder investigation was announced by Robbins LLP in August with no confirmed finding or scheduled step, which is narrative colour rather than a resolved question. The shares at $18.84 sit 14.8% above the 200-day MA of $16.42 and 25.4% below the 52-week high. This suggests a profitable, cash-returning platform compounding steadily rather than inflecting.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the RMB2.41B low end, adjusted operating margin gives back the year-over-year gain, or the buyback pace slows materially.

thesis: Semtech reported fiscal Q2 on Aug 25: revenue of $341.9M, up 32.7% year over year and about 4% above consensus, adjusted EPS of $0.71 against $0.61, improving inventory, and Q3 revenue guidance at a $410M midpoint roughly 14.6% above the $379M analysts expected. Three houses raised targets on the print — Craig Hallum to $205 from $105, UBS to $230 from $225, Morgan Stanley to $195 from $175. The strongest counter-evidence is the pending securities class action alleging management overstated CopperEdge demand across the Nov 2024-Feb 2025 class period, which goes directly to whether guidance from this management can be trusted. It does not change the read here: the 32.7% growth is a delivered result rather than a forward claim, the related shareholder derivative case was dismissed in August 2026, and the target raises came from independent analysts reacting to reported numbers. The shares at $140.85 sit 34.5% above the 200-day MA of $104.75 and 20.6% below the 52-week high. This suggests the disclosed operating trajectory has genuinely inflected.
invalidation: Q3 revenue lands below the $405M low end of guidance, CopperEdge demand commentary is walked back again, or the securities class action produces a scheduled ruling or adverse finding.
sources: Kessler Topaz (SMTC securities class action): https://www.ktmc.com/semtech-corporation/

thesis: SpaceX reported Q2 on Aug 4 with results above expectations, but capital expenditure rose more than sixfold year over year to $18.37B, of which $15.83B went to AI infrastructure following the February xAI merger, and the shares fell 6% after hours. Subsequent reporting adds a planned $100B Starbase spaceport investment in Louisiana, extending rather than moderating that spending profile. The evidence remains genuinely offsetting: revenue growth and a narrowed net loss against a run-rate that produced a $4.9B loss last year, with Starlink connectivity still the only profitable segment, and the shares 39% below their peak. The company listed on Jun 12, 2026, so at 51 real daily bars there is no 200-day trend to judge the drawdown against, and a suit seeking to shut down the gas turbines powering the Colossus 2 data centre puts a $45B Anthropic contract at issue. This suggests the capital-intensity question is unresolved rather than answered by the beat.
invalidation: Capital expenditure guidance moderates while connectivity margins hold, or the Colossus 2 turbine litigation resolves without disrupting the Anthropic contract.

thesis: Marvell reports fiscal Q2 after the close on Aug 27, one day out, with consensus at $0.67 EPS and $2.0095B revenue implying 35.1% year-over-year growth. That is an unresolved binary event falling before any plausible next review, and shares are already trading up in the extended session ahead of it. The disclosed items in hand are the Aug 19 commercial agreement granting Alphabet a warrant over roughly 58.97 million shares, about 7% of shares outstanding, at an exercise price of $206.58 — below the $245.115 close, so upside is shared with the customer from here — alongside a $12.2B custom-chip deal with the same counterparty that investors are looking to the print to size. The stock has nearly tripled in 2026 and sits 67% above its 200-day MA of $146.52, so the 13.5% 60-day pullback is a give-back inside a very extended advance rather than deterioration. This suggests no basis for establishing a position the day before the event that will reprice it.
invalidation: The Aug 27 print and guidance clear expectations and the shares hold their post-print level, at which point the setup can be re-screened with the binary resolved.
sources: StockStory (Aug 27 earnings preview, consensus and Google deal): https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/mrvl/news/earnings/marvell-technology-mrvl-reports-earnings-tomorrow-what-to-expect

thesis: AMD's Q2, reported in the first week of August for the quarter ended Jun 27, beat on both lines at $1.66 EPS against $1.62 and $11.55B revenue against $11.28B, with data-centre revenue more than doubling. The 11.2% 60-day decline is attributed in reporting to a sector-wide semiconductor sell-off on AI-overspending fears rather than to disclosed deterioration at AMD, which is a sentiment-driven explanation and limits how much the drawdown itself should be read as information. Company-specific negatives sit alongside it: a major customer said it would source AI chips from a rival, and warrants over 320 million shares committed to OpenAI and Meta at $0.01, close to 20% of the 1.63 billion shares outstanding, will cap reported EPS as milestones vest — though those were disclosed between October 2025 and February 2026 and none had vested as of late June. The $4.75B raised on Aug 14 was senior unsecured notes maturing 2029-2036, straight debt rather than equity or convertibles, so it adds leverage without diluting holders. Shares at $481.01 sit 44.9% above the 200-day MA of $332.01. This suggests the disclosed fundamentals remain intact while the pullback is sentiment-led.
invalidation: Data-centre revenue growth decelerates on the next print, further major customers move volume to rivals, or warrant vesting milestones are hit in a way that materially resets reported EPS expectations.
